## About Me

::: {.highlight-box}

<div class="home-question">
How should communities plan and invest when today's decisions reshape tomorrow's risk?
</div>

Risk and decisions shape each other over time. I develop computational models and decision methods to understand how hazards, development, public investments, and stakeholder behavior shape future risk and inform effective and equitable resilience decisions.

:::

<div class="job-market-note">
✨ I am on the <strong>2026–2027 academic job market</strong> for faculty positions!
</div>

I am a Postdoctoral Researcher at the [CHEER Hub](https://www.drc.udel.edu/cheer/) within the University of Delaware's Disaster Research Center, working with [Rachel Davidson](https://ccee.udel.edu/faculty/rachel-davidson/) and [Linda Nozick](https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/linda-k-nozick/). I lead development of the Stakeholder-based Tool for the Analysis of Regional Risk (STARR), which simulates how evolving hazards, development, government policies, insurance markets, and household decisions interact over time. My research examines how planning and mitigation policies influence future risk, public expenditures, and the distribution of resilience benefits.

I earned my Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering from Purdue University, advised by [David Johnson](https://engineering.purdue.edu/IE/people/ptProfile?resource_id=126281). My doctoral research developed reinforcement learning and optimization-based methods for adaptive flood risk management under deep uncertainty. I also contributed regional flood-risk analyses to Louisiana's 50-year, $50 billion Coastal Master Plan, working with government agencies, interdisciplinary researchers, and community stakeholders to inform long-term flood protection. Before joining Delaware, I worked as a Senior Flood Engineer at Karen Clark & Company, contributing to large-scale U.S. flood and hurricane catastrophe models.

My work has been recognized through peer-reviewed publications, competitive funding, and professional leadership. I received a competitive **$48,448 NSF–Every Page Foundation Ocean Decade Champion award** as Principal Investigator and served as Chair of the [Engineering and Infrastructure Specialty Group](https://www.sra.org/risk-analysis-specialty-groups/engineering-and-infrastructure/) of the Society for Risk Analysis.

## News

- **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*An Optimization-Based Approach to Developing Computationally Efficient Long-Term Event-Loss Scenario Ensembles*](https://ascelibrary.org/doi/10.1061/AJRUA6.RUENG-2004), is now available in the *ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering*.

- **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*Coupling Land Use Planning and Multi-Stakeholder Dynamics to Inform Disaster Risk Management: Who Pays for Risk and Who Gains from Intervention?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106222), is now available in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*.

- **Jul 2026:** Our paper, [*Direct Policy Search for a Risk-Based Levee Design Framework With Scenario Reduction*](https://doi.org/10.1111/jfr3.70248), was published in the *Journal of Flood Risk Management*.

- **May 2026:** Research spotlight presentation at the NHERI Computational Symposium on computational methods for modeling long-term sequences of hazard losses and their implications for recovery and resilience.

- **May 2026:** Our paper, [*Stakeholder Dynamics in Disaster Mitigation Funding: The Roles of Timing, Spatial Scale and Allocation Basis in Policy Design*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106120), was published in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*.

- **Dec 2025:** Presented first-authored research at the Society for Risk Analysis Annual Meeting on land-use planning and multi-stakeholder disaster risk.
